notes: Static election-security message experiments support bounded survey outcomes; they are indirect evidence for assistant grounding and do not test voting access or disenfranchisement.
The interface experiment supports a bounded acceptance endpoint; it does not test the effect of a legal prohibition or agency transfer.
Observed FMT label non-coverage and evasion constrain the intervention claim; no causal effect on delay, reach, virality, or harm was estimated.
Randomized experiments and a YouTube field study directly support immediate recognition of the specifically taught manipulation techniques.
Offline recommender experiments support bounded minimisation feasibility, not effects of assistant-memory controls on manipulation or dependency.
Partial relevant-data receipt and failed import or direct transfer constrain functional-portability claims; assistant-state exit remains untested.
